dialogues.speaker: Khrustalev
dialogues.text: Ghost stories. Ugh, don't even get me started. Ghost stories these days have no originality at all. It's always the same few formulas.

dialogues.speaker: Khrustalev
dialogues.text: Like an empty train that suddenly pulls in at midnight, and everyone on board insists you stole your own belongings, then drags you off the train. And at the end, they go, "Didn't you notice? No one on that train had feet!"

dialogues.speaker: Khrustalev
dialogues.text: Or it's someone wandering into an empty hospital, an empty castle, an empty house, an empty classroom... Then they hear all kinds of strange noises, listen closely, and realize it's someone who died ages ago muttering to themselves...

dialogues.speaker: Khrustalev
dialogues.text: Readers these days are completely numb to that sort of thing! Forget scaring them. You couldn't even make them laugh with it!

dialogues.speaker: Khrustalev
dialogues.text: At this point, I'll have to go gather some materials myself. I really hope I can find something good, or my story's going to get rejected again...

dialogues.speaker: Khrustalev
dialogues.text: But how am I supposed to get good material when I spend all day selling tickets here?

dialogues.speaker: Khrustalev
dialogues.text: *sigh* You know what, if nothing else works, maybe I'll just sneak onto a train one day or something...
